Here we start with the basics – wrapping up your final affairs.

This will include funeral costs and any lingering medical costs. A reasonable estimate for a typical funeral is around $20,000.

Crazy, right? You can get burial insurance to cover only the most basic of final expenses.

Debt burdens are high in the US, and debt can be especially crushing on remaining family members. Many life insurance customers make sure they can pay off most of their debt with the policy.

Medical costs are a serious variable. Even if you have excellent health insurance, there are likely to be unpaid medical bills lingering after your death. This has to do with copayments, deductibles, and coinsurance provisions.

Collectively, they can add up to many thousands of dollars. But where things get really complicated is if you die of a terminal illness.

It has been revealed that for example, if you are stricken by an illness that lasts for several years, you could incur a number of expenses that are not covered by insurance. This may include the cost of personal care and even experimental treatments.

Recent findings suggest that A home may be a large asset, but it’s also often a homeowner’s largest debt. The average mortgage balance in the US is roughly $236,443 according to Experian data. So you could easily use a life insurance policy to pay off that debt and relieve your loved ones of a monthly mortgage payment.

Sources indicate that credit card debt and other personal debt are some of the most expensive obligations carrying rates upward of 20% in some cases. Make sure you have enough to cover this very expensive debt.

Below is a sampling of major expenses your family is likely to incur, either on an annual basis or at some point after your death.

According to recent reports, tuition costs continue to skyrocket. The Department of Education suggests that four-year public college tuition has been rising an average of 5% per year, far exceeding the rate of inflation. If you have one child who attends an in-state public school, a second at an out-of-state public school, and a third in a private university, the total expenditure will reach $416,560.

It has been revealed that vehicles and other forms of transportation represent another large sum. Unfortunately, with increasing electronics and safety features, the average cost of a new car continues to grow.

If your family relies on your work for healthcare, take notice. According to eHealth.com, the average health insurance premium for a family is $22,221. That’s a shade under $2,000 per month in additional cost. This cost will only rise, and the need could last for years.

So far, we’ve been describing the financial obligations likely to affect a typical household.But there may be certain situations that will produce obligations that are less obvious.

For example, if you’re a business owner, there may be debts or other financial obligations that will need to be paid upon your death.

Even though no one in your family may be qualified or interested in taking over your business, the payoff of those obligations may be completely necessary to enable the sale of the business.

Another possibility is that you’re a real estate investor.

If your properties are heavily indebted, extra insurance proceeds may be necessary either to carry the properties until they’re sold, or even to pay off existing indebtedness to free up cash flow for income.

You may even need additional funds if you are taking care of an extended family member, like an aging parent.

These are just some of the many possibilities of expenses that will need to be covered by insurance proceeds.

Before we move on to specific life insurance quotes, let’s first consider the factors that affect term life insurance premiums.

Recent findings suggest that this is typically the single most key premium factor. The older you are, the more likely you are to die within the term of the policy.

Recent findings suggest that this is a close second and why it’s so vital to apply for a policy as early in life as possible. Premiums on life insurances rates literally increase by each year.

If you have any health conditions that may affect mortality, such as diabetes or hypertension, your premiums will be higher. This is another compelling reason to apply while you are young and in good health.

It’s not that policies are not available to people with health conditions, it’s just that they’re less expensive if you don’t have any.

A 10-year term policy will have a lower premium than a 20-year term policy, which will be lower than a 30-year term. The shorter the term, the less likely it is the insurance company will have to pay a claim before it expires.

According to recent reports, size of the policy matters, but not the way you might think. Yes, a $1 million policy will cost more than a $500,000 policy. But it won’t cost twice as much.

The larger the policy, the lower the per-thousand cost will be.

When the size of the death benefit is considered, the larger policy will always be more cost-effective.

Sources indicate that for example, certain occupations are more hazardous than others (think policeman versus librarian). Deep-sea diving is higher risk than golf. And smoking is the one activity guaranteed to raise your premiums substantially.

With this information in mind, let’s take a look at whether you should consider a $1 million whole life policy instead.

It has been revealed that any discussion on life insurance should include a comparison of whole life and term life insurance coverage. After all, both products can be immensely valuable in the right situation, yet one product (whole life) costs considerably more than the other.

Most of the time, the debate is settled in favor of term life insurance based on cost alone.

A whole life insurance policy can easily cost 10x the same amount of coverage you can get with a term policy.

With that being noted, whole life insurance and other investment-type life insurance coverage can be valuable in terms of the cash value you can build up over time. Whole life insurance also offers a fixed benefit amount for your heirs that will last for your entire life, yet the cost of your premiums are guaranteed to stay the same.

Recent findings suggest that the cash value of a whole life insurance policy also grows on a tax-deferred basis, and you can borrow against this amount if you need a loan. Further, many whole life policies from reputable providers also pay out dividends during good years, which can be substantial.

The problem with whole life and other similar policies like universal life is the fact that premiums can be exorbitant for the amount of coverage you might need.

A couple with young children provides a good example since they might need a $1 million dollar policy or more to provide income protection for their working years and have money left for college tuition and other expenses.

With young families, expenses are already high.

This includes costs for food for a family, childcare, heavy use of health care, and the seemingly endless demand for clothing, furniture, and even entertainment as the children grow.

As you can see from the cost comparison below from State Farm, there’s not enough room in the typical family budget to afford the type of life insurance that’s needed.

A 40-year-old mother and breadwinner in excellent health would pay $80.09 per month for a term life policy that lasts 20 years, whereas a whole life policy in the same amount would cost $1,266.69 per month (or $14,560 annually).

Recent findings suggest that this is a classic situation where term insurance rides to the rescue. The family can afford to buy the amount of coverage they need at an affordable price, whereas paying for permanent life insurance coverage in the same amount would be difficult to justify.

And just as crucial for people of any age and in any circumstance, the extra funds not being spent on insurance premiums can be invested to gradually improve your financial situation.

So absolutely, term insurance will work best for most people.

Following these steps will help you get the best possible rate on a million-dollar life insurance policy.

No one likes to think about their death, but it’s crucial to have a life insurance policy in place in case something happens to you. A million-dollar life insurance policy can give you and your loved one’s peace of mind knowing that they will be taken care of financially if something happens to you.

In a recent development, there is no one-size-fits-all answer to this question, as the best policy for you will depend on your specific needs and preferences. However, some of the top providers of million-dollar life insurance policies include AIG, Banner Life, and Prudential. So be sure to explore your options and compare quotes from different providers before making a decision.

Recent findings suggest that yes, insurance companies offer million-dollar insurance policies with no medical exam. However, the premiums for these policies are typically much higher than for policies with a medical exam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Give a used wheelchair, walker, or shower chair to a program that cleans it and passes it to someone who needs it, such as your state’s assistive technology program or a local loan closet. Return anything Medicare or another insurer still rents to its supplier, oxygen equipment included, since it isn’t yours to give.

Recent findings suggest that in fiscal 2025, state assistive technology programs got 104,257 reused devices to 68,164 people, saving them about $36 million, according to the Center for Assistive Technology Act Data Assistance. More than half were mobility, seating, and positioning devices.

In a recent development, programs like these clean and repair a donated wheelchair or walker, then lend or give it to someone who needs it, often for free. Many thrift stores won’t take medical equipment at all, and Goodwill of Northern Upcoming England lists hospital beds, wheelchairs, and walkers among the donations it can’t accept.

Industry observers note that before you give anything away, make sure it’s yours. Under Medicare, most equipment starts out rented, many wheelchairs included, and ownership usually passes to the patient after 13 months of rental payments, according to the Medicare Rights Center. Oxygen equipment never becomes the patient’s, since under Medicare’s oxygen rules the supplier owns it for the whole five-year cycle and takes it back once it’s no longer needed. Anything still rented, through Medicare or another insurer, goes back to its supplier, and the University of Michigan’s medical equipment service warns that the rental charges can keep coming until it does.

What’s yours can go to one of these, each with its own rules:.

Sources indicate that deducting any of these gifts follows IRS Publication 526’s rules for noncash gifts. You can deduct one only if you itemize, and only at its fair market value, what a willing buyer would pay for it used. A gift to a person, such as one you arrange through an exchange listing, doesn’t count. The new deduction for people who don’t itemize, which starts with 2026 returns, covers cash gifts only. Everything else, from cleaning and testing each item to getting a receipt, works as it does for donating any used stuff.

If you’re clearing out a whole house, its furniture, clothes, books, and old computers each go to groups of their own.

Recent findings suggest that call any of these before you load the car, since their rules on hospital beds and breathing machines differ widely. The loan closet in Howard County, Maryland, refuses hospital beds, CPAP and BiPAP machines, and oxygen concentrators, and REquipment takes no hospital beds. A home hospital bed that nobody near you will take can still go to Project C.U.R.E., which ships it to a clinic abroad.

Are you trying to win the Mega Millions, but your numbers never seem to come up? It may be time to look for better ways to make money. Fortunately, you can earn extra cash without going and getting a “real job.”.

According to recent reports, what are the best ways to avoid sitting in a cubicle all day? Some money-making strategies require an upfront investment, while others let you earn money in your free time with the help of apps.

Read on to learn the best ways to earn cash without a regular 9-5 job, plus tips on how almost anyone can get started.

Industry observers note that one of the easiest ways to earn money is by signing up to participate in market research studies. You won’t make much, a few dollars here and there, but you can create a free account and get started within minutes.

You’ll be paid in PayPal cash or gift cards for sharing your opinion and completing other tasks online.

E-Poll Market Research is one of the top companies to consider for this type of work. They make it easy to create an account and answer survey questions.

However, there are plenty of other options to consider, including:.

While market research gigs won’t make you rich, it’s something you can do during your spare time.

Industry observers note that if you have a book idea, turning your story into an eBook can help you earn passive income without a regular job. Kindle Direct Publishing can even help you format your book for Kindle, at which point you can market and sell your book to millions of potential readers who shop on Amazon.com.

Industry observers note that how much can you earn writing eBooks? That depends on how many books you write, how much you sell them for, and how successful you are at marketing your book. Selling 20 books per month with a profit of $7 per book would net you $140 per month and $1,680 per year.

Meanwhile, selling 100 books per month at $7 per book would net you $700 per month and $8,400 per year. Need a little inspiration? Here’s an article that shows you how to make your first $1,000 selling eBooks.

You can earn a lot of money by starting a blog or niche website and monetizing it. I should know. I started Good Financial Cents more than a decade ago, and have earned millions of dollars through the monetization of this site since its earliest days.

In a recent development, how do you make money blogging? Earning real income with a website isn’t as easy as it looks, but there are plenty of monetization strategies you can try.

Here are the most common ways blogs make money:.

If you’re curious about what it takes to earn money blogging, consider signing up for my Make 1K Challenge. It’s free and can help you earn your first $1,000 online with some of the blog monetization strategies I’ve already mentioned.

You could argue that freelance work is like a regular job, but working at home and on your terms is much different from traditional employment. The fact is, most freelancers are fully remote – they can work from anywhere in the world with a laptop and an internet connection.

According to recent reports, plus, they can hire and fire clients based on their personal needs and preferences, and their income potential is unlimited. According to ZipRecruiter, freelancers in the U.S. average $63.53 per hour.

Of course, you’ll need a marketable skill to find paid work as a freelancer. This could be freelance writing, design skills, marketing expertise, or something else.

You can use several websites to market your skills as a freelancer, including:.

Industry observers note that healthyWage makes it possible to earn money while you lose weight. You won’t earn a ton of cash through the app, but you can earn a few dollars and use it to supplement other income you have.

The more weight you lose, the more money you can make. For example, the HealthyWage website claims some of their clients who lost more than 100 pounds managed to earn anywhere from $1,400 to $3,000.

However, the HW weight loss calculator demonstrates potential earnings of $578 to $828 for people who only have 15 pounds to lose.

In a recent development, if you have a car you rarely use and want to earn some side income, you can consider renting it out with Turo, a ride-sharing platform that connects car owners with people who need a short-term rental. You can set your price, although you’ll have more success if you price your car competitively.

Nicer vehicles in high-demand areas can easily fetch rates that surpass $100 per day through this platform. Turo notes that in-demand cars rented out regularly can bring in anywhere from $10,000 to $20,000 per year in net profit.

Recent findings suggest that plus, almost anyone can rent out their car provided it meets the guidelines of the Turo platform. Your car must be 12 years old or newer with less than 130,000 miles. It must be worth less than $200,000 (no Lambo’s), and you must also meet Turo’s auto insurance requirements.

Do you have a spare bedroom in your home that you never use? Maybe you have a basement or garage apartment you could fix up and begin renting for a profit?

In a recent development, either way, Airbnb lets you rent out rooms and other spaces in your home on any dates you prefer. You must let renters know they’re renting a room in a home vs. an entire apartment or house and provide as much additional detail as possible.

Industry observers note that the amount you can earn will depend on where you live and the type of accommodation you can offer. However, expensive cities like Chicago, Fresh York, and San Francisco have plenty of rooms for rent that go for well over $100 per night.

You may not have an entire room you can rent, but even if you have some storage space, Neighbor.com allows you to rent it out to others in need.

Common spaces rented through this platform include.

Recent findings suggest that the Neighbor.com platform makes it easy to advertise your unused space so that people nearby can inquire if they’re interested. Also, note that the platform offers insurance that can protect you if some of your client’s items are damaged or stolen while in your care.

Sources indicate that how much can you make renting out extra space? It depends on how much space you have to rent and where it’s located. However, Neighbor.com demonstrates a range of rental space options that cost anywhere from $20 to $100+ per month.

Investing in dividend stocks is one of the best ways to earn money without a regular job. Many early retirees find a way to live and pay bills based solely on the dividends they receive from various stocks.

But what exactly is a dividend stock? For the most part, they are regular stocks but with a track record of sharing their profits with investors through dividends.

Dividends can also be earned in exchange-traded funds (ETFs) or mutual funds, and they can be significant once you build up a large portfolio.

Recent findings suggest that since dividends are paid by profitable companies, they tend to be seen as less risky for investors. If you’re curious about what it takes to get started with this strategy, this post explains how to invest in dividend stocks.

Housesitting is an option if you’re somewhat mobile and can move from place to place. Generally, you can find house-sitting gigs through word of mouth, referrals, or online portals like Craigslist.org or Facebook Marketplace.

That stated, not all house-sitting gigs are paid. Some offer the potential for exotic travel instead and free lodging for a week to several months.

In a recent development, either way, a website called TrustedHousesitters is the best place to find house-sitting gigs. Some jobs posted are for house-sitting only, while others require house sitters to provide basic care for pets or plants.

Industry observers note that if you have serious wanderlust and want to travel far and wide, this platform can help make it happen. Many gigs posted online are in countries like Australia, Ireland, France, and Switzerland.

If you love animals and want to earn money taking care of them, several platforms can help turn your dream into a reality.

For example, Rover.com lets you provide basic care for dogs or cats in your home, or you can pick up dog walking gigs. Another mobile app, called Wag!, lets you do more of the same.

You can set your rates for all types of work through these platforms, and your availability. While earnings vary by location and job, most people watch dogs and cats for anywhere from $40 to $100 per night.

Industry observers note that real estate investing may seem like a pipe dream if you hope to earn income without a job but hear me out. There are many ways to earn income through real estate without owning physical property or dealing with the hassles of being a landlord.

You can invest in real estate investment trusts (REITs) that let you build wealth over time. You can also use a platform called Fundrise to invest in real estate with a minimum investment of $10.

Fundrise lets you purchase eREITs, large investment funds that acquire, own, or operate multi-residential and commercial properties. The income you earn is entirely passive since it handles the work of finding income-producing properties and managing them.

Industry observers note that while returns are never guaranteed, Fundrise investors have achieved very solid returns. Investors who use the platform earned an average return of 7.31% in 2020, followed by 22.99% in 2021, 1.50% in 2022 and -7.45% in 2023 (their first down year).

Recent findings suggest that you can earn income on your spare change by investing it using Acorns. The roundup savings app syncs to your debit or credit card rounds up every purchase you make to the nearest dollar, and invests the difference. Once it’s set up, there’s no work on your part.

It has been revealed that most of the money is invested in ETFs and managed by the world’s top investment firms like Vanguard and BlackRock. While this app makes it easy to invest small amounts of money, it’s not free to use. Personal intends start at $3 per month, while a family strategy costs just $5.

If you’re looking for some paid gigs that are relatively easy, consider setting up a profile on TaskRabbit, an online platform that lets you get paid for completing various tasks, such as:.

Projects typically pay between $30 and $100, although some pay significantly more than that. TaskRabbit also lets you pick and choose the jobs you want to take on based on your availability so that you can work entirely on your schedule.

If you love taking photographs and have a knack for getting professional-looking images, you can use your skills and expertise to sell photos online.

Websites like Depositphotos and iStockPhoto pay photographers to supply them with stock photos they can sell to writers, publications, and various online platforms.

Industry observers note that the best part about this side hustle is that you can get started with the equipment you already have. While you can use a professional camera if you want to, many smartphones take professional-quality photos.

Recent findings suggest that earning a bank bonus is another way to earn money without a regular job, but you’ll need an upfront investment to get started. Most bonus offers require you to deposit a specific amount of money and keep it in your account for up to 12 months.

You may also be required to set up direct deposit to earn a bank bonus, and other terms and conditions may apply.

Where can you find the best bank bonuses? While bonus offers constantly change, you can start by checking with banks like Chase, HSBC, Radius Bank, and Wells Fargo.

Flipping furniture requires some upfront legwork and potentially even some artistic talent, but you can earn a solid income with this strategy if you know what you’re doing.

Essentially, this side hustle requires you to shop at thrift stores, garage sales, and online platforms to find furniture that will ultimately sell for more than you paid.

From there, you can sell the furniture as-is or clean it up and paint it with the goal of fetching an even higher price.

You can make money driving for Uber or Lyft on your own time, picking and choosing the days and hours you want to work.

Not only is rideshare work one of the most flexible side hustles, but you can earn $20 per hour and more with tips.

If you are low on free time but still want to make money without a job, consider selling stuff you don’t need. An array of online platforms makes it a breeze, although some platforms work better for selling.

For example, you can use Poshmark to earn money selling used clothing and accessories, while used electronics tend to sell best on platforms like eBay.com, Decluttr, BuyBackWorld, and Gazelle.

If you have home decor, furniture, or workout equipment to sell, you’ll almost always do better unloading those items locally on Facebook Marketplace.

Starting a YouTube channel is another way to earn money without a job, but that doesn’t mean it’s not work. The fact is, that creating quality videos and building an audience takes a lot of creativity and time. Plus, not everyone who tries to build a YouTube channel will succeed.

Sources indicate that that stated, you can earn income without a regular job. I know because I have done it with my YouTube channel, Wealth Hacker.

How much you can earn on YouTube varies quite a bit, but it’s possible to earn thousands of dollars per month. If you’re curious about monetizing videos, my in-depth guide will show you how to make money on YouTube.

In a recent development, donating plasma is a unique way to earn money without a job, although it’s not very glamorous. DonatingPlasma.org makes it easy to find plasma donation centers in your area, and you can earn as much as $100 for your first donation.

Industry observers note that that mentioned, subsequent plasma donations typically earn closer to $50. You’ll also be limited by the number of times you can donate plasma within a month. However, it’s possible to use this side gig to earn an extra $500 per month, which you can use to supplement your primary income.

Recent findings suggest that if you are willing to complete various tasks that help regular workers do their jobs, consider becoming a crowd worker. This gig will have you finishing up to-do lists of jobs that don’t require specific technical skills.

For example, you may get paid to proofread documents, label images, patch a resume, complete a form, or complete a data entry assignment.

Several platforms help you find crowd-working gigs, but the best ones include Microworkers and Clickworker.

Sources indicate that if you want to do something simple that will get you moving, consider delivering groceries using apps like Instacart or Shipt. You get paid hourly, plus tips and all you have to do is head to the store, purchase groceries according to a list, and deliver them to people in your neighborhood.

The gig is extremely flexible, similar to driving for Uber or Lyft.

Industry observers note that another non-job gig lets you get paid to deliver packages for Amazon.com. You can do this through a platform called Amazon Flex, which promises its drivers anywhere from $18 to $25 per hour.

Unlike a regular Amazon job, Flex lets you pick the day and the hours you want to work. To get started, you need to create a free account, get approved, and start reserving blocks of time you want to deliver packages.

Finally, you can earn money by selling unwanted or unused gift cards in your possession. This hustle is made easy thanks to platforms like GiftDeals.com and CardCash.com.

Industry observers note that you won’t get the total value of your gift cards, but you should get 90% or more of the gift card balance for each card you sell. While selling gift cards for less than their total value may not seem ideal, it’s better than not using them and getting nothing in return.

It has been revealed that finally, you can earn small amounts of money by signing up with the best online survey sites. Not only is this side hustle as easy as it gets, but you can participate and get paid during your spare time and even on your phone.

Other online survey sites to check out include the following:.

There you have it, 26 ways to make money without a job. While many of the jobs on our list won’t replace your 9-5, they can be a great way to increase your income so you can pay off debt or break the cycle of living paycheck to paycheck.

Compare Savings Accounts by the Rate You’ll Keep – It’s in the Fine Print

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, before you open a high-yield savings account, compare the rate your balance will still earn six months from now, not the one advertised.
  • In a recent development, when one bank’s “up to” rate tops another’s plain rate, the fine print explains the gap.
  • Take two sample accounts, each holding $10,000 for a year, with the interest left in.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, before you open a high-yield savings account, compare the rate your balance will still earn six months from now, not the one advertised. Read the bank’s fine print for a boost that ends, a balance tier or cap, monthly conditions, fees, and limits on getting your money out.

In a recent development, when one bank’s “up to” rate tops another’s plain rate, the fine print explains the gap. The higher number is the bank’s best case, and your balance may earn it for only a few months, or not at all.

Take two sample accounts, each holding $10,000 for a year, with the interest left in. Each rate is an APY, the annual percentage yield, which includes the interest your interest earns. One pays 4.35% for six months and 4.00% after, and earns about $417 in the first year. The other pays a plain 4.40% and earns $440.

It has been revealed that in a rate table, 4.35% and 4.40% look like a tie. After the boost, the plain account’s 4.40% earns about $40 a year more on $10,000 than the other’s 4.00%, and more on a bigger balance.

It has been revealed that federal Truth in Savings rules require a bank’s online ad that quotes an APY to state any minimum balance needed to earn it. Read these five terms on the rate page and in the account’s disclosures before you compare high-yield savings accounts.

Industry observers note that last, search for the bank on the FDIC’s BankFind, or for a credit union on the NCUA’s Credit Union Locator, to confirm your deposits are federally insured. Money in an app that isn’t a bank is insured only through its partner bank, so search for that bank instead.

Start your short list with the best high-yield savings accounts.

Having more than one type of debt is common, and that’s especially true once you graduate from college and start your first “real job.” You may have credit card debt, an auto loan, and a mortgage payment to make once you buy your first home. It’s also common to have other random debts to cover, including student loans.

In a recent development, if you’re like many who took out loans during college, you will likely be paying them off after you graduate. In fact, 82% of students who borrowed loans expect to be making payments post-graduation, according to a recent College Ave Student Loans survey.

That remarked, you’ll want to make sure you’re balancing debt repayment with your savings goals along the way.

Recent findings suggest that you’ll also want to make sure you’re paying down debts in the optimal order, or in a way that will help you save the most money on interest as possible while aligning with your goals. Which debts should you pay off first? Here’s a rundown of how to get the best results:.

In a recent development, no matter which types of debt you have, credit card debt should be your first priority. Why? Because credit card debt is likely the most expensive debt you have by far.

Federal Reserve data shows the average credit card interest rate on accounts assessed interest came in at around 22% as of May 2023, yet your credit card could easily be charging higher rates than the average.

Sources indicate that to save as much money as possible, you should strive to pay as much as you can toward high-interest credit card bills each month. You can also pay down credit card debt faster with the help of a debt consolidation loan or a 0% APR balance transfer credit card.

Other unsecured debts like personal loan debt should come next in the debt payoff pecking order. After all, unsecured debts tend to have higher interest rates than secured debts like auto loans. In fact, the Federal Reserve also reported that the average interest rate on a 24-month personal loan came in at 11.48% as of May 2023, compared to the average rate of 7.81% on a 60-month auto loan.

Ideally, you’ll start paying more toward personal loan debt and other unsecured debts after all credit card debt is entirely paid off, although you should make at least the minimum payment on all your bills throughout the entire process.

The next debt you’ll want to tackle is your student loans. I suggest focusing on these loans after other unsecured debts, since federal student loans (and many private student loans) come with low fixed interest rates and monthly payments that will not change over time. If you have federal student loans, you may even want to look into income-driven repayment intends.

According to recent reports, if you’re hoping to pay down student loans faster or just want to save money on interest, you can also consider refinancing your student loans to get a shorter repayment timeline, a lower monthly payment, or both. Just remember that refinancing federal student loans can mean losing access to income-driven repayment aims and federal protections like deferment and forbearance.

Once you have paid off or substantially paid down all your other debts, you can focus your efforts on secured debts you have like mortgage loans and auto loans. These debts should be dealt with last since they are secured with collateral and tend to offer lower interest rates as a result. For example, you can consider paying more than the minimum on your mortgage, a car loan, or both until they’re paid off completely.

Then again, you may want to pay off debts with extremely low interest rates as slowly as possible to free up more cash flow for living expenses and investments. If you took out a mortgage in January of 2021 when the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed rate home loan was as low as 2.65%, for example, it makes sense to make the minimum payment on that debt and invest your extra cash instead.

In a recent development, it’s crucial to make sure you balance debt repayment with other financial considerations. After all, focusing too much on debt repayment early in life can leave you behind when it comes to investing for retirement or saving up for a first home.

While you’ll want to eliminate credit card debt and other high-interest debts as quickly as you can, even if you have to stop saving and investing for a while, you can pay down student loan debt and secured debts at a slower pace while saving and investing for the future along the way.

Industry observers note that finally, make sure you have adequate emergency savings throughout your entire debt payoff journey, or that you begin saving for emergencies as soon as you can. Without a fully funded emergency fund, you can end up relying on credit cards and other loans to get by and ruin your debt payoff progress in the process.

How much should you save? While most experts recommend having an emergency fund that can cover three to six months of expenses, it’s okay to start small if you have to.

Having more than one type of debt is how it works for most people, especially when you’re young and in the early stages of your career. When it comes to paying it off, however, you’ll want to make sure you have a concrete proposal that can help you reduce interest charges and get where you want to be.

In a recent development, focusing on credit card debt and other unsecured debts first always makes sense, since these debts aren’t secured by an asset and tend to charge much higher interest rates. You can focus on student loans next, followed by other secured debts you have like a home loan or car loan.

Sources indicate that in the meantime, make sure you have an adequate emergency fund and invest in it for retirement. After all, debt won’t last forever if you’re serious about repayment, and saving and investing early can help you benefit from compound interest and avoid using credit cards for surprise expenses. Creating a budget to track these factors is your best bet.

If you need help creating one, or simply don’t know where to start, use this budget worksheet as your guide – you’ll reach financial freedom in no time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that australian grain farm manager Scott Gladman, 63, is attempting to swim the length of the Darling River, Australia’s third-longest river. It begins in Latest South Wales and finishes at its confluence with the Murray River at Wentworth. Gladman believes he will be the first person to swim the entire 1,650km route.

Recent findings suggest that gladman started on September 1 from near Brewarrina in far north Newly introduced South Wales. At the outset, he budgeted 103 days to complete the swim, averaging around 16km per day. So far, he is largely on track. After 49 days, he has covered 660km, leaving just under 1,000km to go.

Interestingly, the expedition is not born from a love of endurance swimming. Gladman was inspired to find a fundraising challenge to support friends impacted by Motor Neuron Disease and Progressive Supranuclear Palsy, a rare form of Parkinson’s. Initially, he considered the Murray. “I just thought I could swim the Murray River, but people have done that,” he told ABC News. “No one has had a crack at the Darling.”.

According to recent reports, the location of the Darling River in Australia. Photo: Wikimedia Commons.

Gladman gave himself 18 months to train. In the summer, he swam in the Murray River at Boundary Bend, Victoria, and during winter he completed laps in indoor pools. Now out on the Darling, a support boat of family and friends keeps him organization, alongside a canoeist.

“There’s no real form of communication, and I wear earplugs…he’ll [the canoeist] either have to hit me on the back of the head with a paddle to get my attention, or he’ll just start steering toward me, and that will push me one way or the other,” Gladman said.

In a recent development, despite its length, the Darling River is sometimes so shallow that Gladman needs to float through sections on his back, or walk. The support boat also sometimes requires saving, with Gladman having to help clear a path through river debris:.

How Unlimited Free Stuff from Amazon Almost Ruined My Retirement

📅 07 Oct 2025 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2020 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It all started last winter when I innocently posted a review for a heated vest I had bought on Amazon.
  • You’ve been selected to join Amazon Vine for writing helpful reviews!”.
  • I was already aware of Amazon Vine since I had seen product reviews from other people in the program – typically called “Vine Voices.” The basic idea of this program is that you can order stuff from Amazon for free, as long as you agree to review at least 80% of the things you order.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It all started last winter when I innocently posted a review for a heated vest I had bought on Amazon. I was happy with this fun latest way to beat the winter and wanted to share it with others, so I gave it five stars. But soon after I clicked “Submit”, I got an email from Amazon which stated something like,.

“Congratulations! You’ve been selected to join Amazon Vine for writing helpful reviews!”.

I was already aware of Amazon Vine since I had seen product reviews from other people in the program – typically called “Vine Voices.” The basic idea of this program is that you can order stuff from Amazon for free, as long as you agree to review at least 80% of the things you order.

“Hey, that’s cool”, I thought, “Who doesn’t like free stuff?

Especially since I’ve already been writing product reviews out of the goodness of my heart – why not be rewarded for it?”.

So without giving it much further thought, I clicked “accept” on their terms and conditions and joined the program.

And so began a saga that has taken me on a surprising journey over the past nine months causing me to:.

It has been revealed that okay, I’ll admit that there were also some upsides. My original idea was partly to save some money, by getting stuff I genuinely would have bought anyway, in a way that sounded fun. And that did happen – I saved at least a few thousand dollars on tools and materials for my construction business and the MMM-HQ Coworking space, for free. Plus, at least some of the motivation for signing up was to put myself through an experiment so I could write this blog article about it. And if you’re reading this, it looks like that happened too.

But I was still surprised at how powerful the combination of small nudges and incentives from Amazon was able to hijack my frugality instincts –  and get me to do a bunch of work that wasn’t really the best use of my time.

Recent findings suggest that so I figured if we review my journey and break it down with a bit of Behavioral Science, we could all learn a few valuable things by laughing at Mr. Money Mustache’s folly.

Scarcity Brain and the Online Casino Effect.

Sources indicate that one of the most interesting books I’ve read in recent years is Michael Easter’s Scarcity Brain. It’s an exploration of the sneaky ways that modern gambling platforms, marketing and social media algorithms are all built upon two weaknesses in our evolutionary programming:.

As I look back now, I realize that I fell straight into those same traps, because the Vine program has all the key properties of a casino or a TikTok feed:.

But occasionally, there will be genuinely useful things like super nice light fixtures, tools and plumbing parts, an EV charger, and even some clothing. My favorite ridiculous Eagle shirt as featured in the Mustachianism music video was an Amazon Vine find.

As were a whole supply of super-realistic artificial plants, which while tacky in principle, have been amazing for hard-to-water courtyard garden areas at the MMM HQ.

Industry observers note that I also had a lot of fun roping in friends and coworkers from HQ to help and share in the bounty. I let them help me request and review stuff that they wanted, and then they got to keep it. This seemed like a win/win because we shared the work and the fun of laughing at some of the ridiculous products available.

Still, as I went through this experiment this spring and summer and allowed the system to coax me into doing 80 reviews so I could upgrade my account from Vine Silver to Vine Gold*, I noticed something didn’t feel quite right.

I was checking the Vine page every day for scores, even when I didn’t actually need anything. It would usually be a bust, but just often enough, something I actually wanted would come up, and I’d order it before it was too late. Scarcity and unpredictable rewards at work.

Industry observers note that then the bounty would come, I’d unpack it and photograph it with assembly-line speed so I could batch-write all the reviews once per week or so. For every review I did, I was spending time I’d rather spend doing something else. And for every questionable item I got, I was creating pollution and trash from its manufacturing and packaging – directly contradicting the main values of my life and my reason for writing this blog. And I saw all of this, yet I kept doing it!

So Was This The Downfall of MMM?

During the worst of this consumerism bender, things were dire. I was getting packages almost every day and my recycling bin was overflowing with cardboard. My son and my girlfriend started laughing at some of my more frivolous purchases, so I found myself discreetly tucking away the boxes when they were around to evade scrutiny.

But eventually, I moved into a recovery stage. I had been letting this habit continue out of laziness and as a form of procrastination: it’s very easy to order shit online and pretend I’m doing something useful, and much more difficult to get moving to do the things that really make my life enjoyable.

But I’m old enough to know that hitting the running trails and the gym for my daily workouts, and making progress on all my construction projects, and focusing on the computer as a creative tool rather than an entertainment device so I can get stuff done like this blog post, are the things that bring me the most joy.

It has been revealed that admittedly, some of the sucky factors of the Vine program helped make it easier to recover too. For every genuinely useful thing I found like a contractor-grade extension cord, I had to scan through endless screens of trinkets which not only wasted my time but actually pissed me off at their very existence.

I also noticed some of the deliberately reviewer-unfriendly features built into the program which reminded me that we reviewers are definitely just low-wage workers rather than any form of VIP. The search functionality is crap, and there is no way to filter or sort the results, because they want you to have to look through everything and they don’t care about the value of your time.

Then there is the hilariously bureaucratic AI-based evaluation system which would occasionally flag my totally tame, factual reviews as “Not meeting our Community Standards” without explaining what the problem was. So I’d have to go in and edit my review, randomly changing a couple of words and maybe some punctuation, and suddenly the AI would be pacified and accept my review. Just dumb.

This is What “Fuck You Money” is For!

It dawned on me that for many people, this is just what “work” looks like. You are given a bunch of tasks and a bunch of rules to follow, in a system you didn’t create and don’t get much say in changing. And then as long as you crank out your TPS Reports without rocking the boat too much, you get your paycheck.

It reminded me of the Uber Driving experiment I did way back in 2017: as soon as I started working as a driver, I could immediately see dozens of improvements that could be made to the system that would make it function better for both drivers and passengers. But since I wasn’t the boss, nobody wanted to hear my ideas.

Industry observers note that experiences like these remind me that while I love hard work and I love learning new things every day, I greatly prefer being the boss. And I’ve gotten pretty damned accustomed to it after 20 years of financial independence, so I see no need to give it up.

One interesting “gotcha” of the Vine program is that they do keep track of all the free stuff you get and send you a 1099 for its retail value at the end of the year. So it’s not really free, just discounted to whatever your marginal tax rate is (about 25% for me this year). If we peek into my account right now, this is how my 2025 is looking:.

So I got about $7000 worth of stuff, and could owe up to $1750 of tax on it. In my case, about 75% of it was “sold” to my business for commercial use (construction supplies which I used on jobs or HQ renovations) so it was effectively converted into real income rather than just tax burden. Some of it was stuff I would have bought anyway for my own house which I’ll gladly pay the taxes on. But there is also probably about $1000 of pure nonsense in there as well, for which I’ll owe a tax bill of $250 as penance for my itchy trigger finger on that “Order” button.

Thanks to some advice from wise readers in the comments (below), I have since learned that in most cases you can mark down this estimated value by 80% before declaring it – because you have effectively eliminated most of the resale value by opening and reviewing the product. Thus my tax bill will be more like $50 rather than $250. More detail in this Reddit discussion here.

So here we are today. While I admit that I didn’t explicitly cancel my account, I used the “Keystone Habit” trick to override the temptation to view the Vine page – mapping that browser bookmark to my daily habits list instead, a little chart which I call my “Badassity Tracker”. The net result is that every time I click it, I’m taken straight to a reminder to get up from the computer and do a quick round of exercise, so I do that instead.

And of course my writing of this article may be a violation of the terms and conditions of the program (“the first rule of Vine is to not talk about Vine”), so it might even get canceled on me. (and if so I’ll let you know because that would be funny story as well).

But I learned a lot about habits and addiction, and realized that this same feeling might be what drives people into One More Year Syndrome, as they keep working even when they can afford to quit. I have now coached enough people through this situation to see it is way more common than I would have ever guessed.

Recent findings suggest that as with all MMM articles, there’s a real life lesson in this story. It’s not really about Vine or me or my habits, it’s about you continuing to look at yourself and your life, and always questioning your own assumptions or patterns. And asking the people you trust most for feedback as well:.

We will never be perfect, but the great news is we don’t have to be. All it takes is a little bit of self reflection and putting ourselves on a slightly better path, as often as we can as life goes on. We are all on a very long journey, so even a tiny course correction can make a huge difference in where we end up.

*(Vine Gold is not all that useful as it turns out as 99.9% of the available items seem to be the same trinkets you see in the Silver tier).

Seven Alpine-Style Climbs Happening Now in Nepal

📅 20 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (620 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that several small teams are attempting difficult climbs on Nepal’s 6,000 and 7,000m peaks.
  • This is what we know about the ongoing expeditions:.
  • Three young French climbers, members of the Military High Mountain Group from Chamonix, celebrated their organization’s 50th anniversary with a new route on Peak 41.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that several small teams are attempting difficult climbs on Nepal’s 6,000 and 7,000m peaks. Unfortunately, they rarely report on their aims or progress until they return, and often only if they succeed.

This is what we know about the ongoing expeditions:.

Three young French climbers, members of the Military High Mountain Group from Chamonix, celebrated their organization’s 50th anniversary with a new route on Peak 41. This 6,654m mountain is located in the Khumbu region and is often called the “true Mera Peak.”.

According to recent reports, konrad Piontek, Amaury Fouillade, and Clovis Paulin took advantage of a good weather window and achieved the first ascent of the peak’s northeast face. They climbed in an alpine-style single push over four days. The result is a beautiful 1,400m line with difficulties up to ED+ 5+ M6 A1 90°. They descended via the southeast face. The team named their line Bon Matin (good morning).

Nivel Meroi and Romano Benet are acclimatized and ready to attempt a new route on Jugal II, but the Italian couple will be on their own. Tine Cuder of Slovenia, the third team member, has left due to illness.

Meanwhile, in the Kangchenjunga region, a large Russian team has also finished acclimatizing. The team trekked in the area and crossed a number of high-altitude passes, the latest of them at the top of an icefall at 5,750m. They reported lots of snow above 5,000m but are ready to attempt a new route on the formidable Jannu (7,710m) from its southeast side.

The team comprises Ivan Artemov, Ivan Volkov, Artem Zhdanov, Konstantin Neumoin, Roman Shilin, and Vasily Yagodin.

Hidesuke Taneishi and Tetsu Hashimoto of Japan traveled to Nepal in September, aiming to achieve the first ascent of Gangapurna West (7,455m), also known as Asapurna or Peak Lachenal. They have provided no news since, but they probably had to retreat when an intense snowstorm hit the Annapurna region three weeks ago.

Location of Gangapurna West on a Google Earth screenshot. Notes by Lindsay Griffin for the American Alpine Journal.

Meanwhile, a second team has reached the base of the peak with the same objective. Valery Shamalo, Natalia Zanina, Maksim Trufanov, and Ruslan Kirichenko arrived at the beginning of October and saw no one else there. They reported that recent precipitation had left the trail in a poor state; the climbers had to cross landslides and swollen rivers to reach base camp.

The team has completed two acclimatization climbs, looking for a passage through the icefall at the base of the mountain and then a series of couloirs. They reached 5,900m and, on a second trip, 6,600m. Deep snow covered the peak, which slowed progress. Finally, they introduced a summit bid last week.

From 6,600m, they spent a day on technical ice sections of 70–80º. In poor visibility, they endured spindrift and were showered by small ice chunks.

“In the afternoon, the weather deteriorated sharply,” Natalia Zanina stated. “Heavy snowfall began, and we started being struck by large, continuous avalanches. At 6,800m (340m from the summit), we decided to turn back.”.

A note on names: according to 8000ers.com, Asapurna should be the correct name for this peak because — although it is closer to Gangapurna — Asapurna’s summit ridge connects directly to Annapurna III.

Sources indicate that the list of climbing permits granted by Nepal’s Ministry of Tourism points to some other interesting expeditions, some of them in remote western Nepal. There is a permit for Nyalu Kang (6,265m), only opened to foreign climbers in 2024 and reportedly unclimbed, and Ardang, summited once by Canadians Bryce Kendall and Sunny Twelker in 2019. Victor Saunders and Mick Fowler of the UK attempted Ardang last year.

Animal Attack Roundup, Oct. 20

📅 20 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (714 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As we pointed out last week, most victims of animal attacks around the world are not tourists but the people who live amid potentially dangerous animals all the time.
  • Photo: Ludovic Laude/L’Est Republicain.
  • A normally timid mountain ungulate has been attacking runners on the outskirts of Besançon in eastern France.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As we pointed out last week, most victims of animal attacks around the world are not tourists but the people who live amid potentially dangerous animals all the time. Here are some incidents that have come to light recently.

Chamois in France. Photo: Ludovic Laude/L’Est Republicain.

A normally timid mountain ungulate has been attacking runners on the outskirts of Besançon in eastern France.

One victim, a 30-year-old woman jogger, was knocked unconscious and suffered a punctured shoulder and serious scalp wounds requiring stitches and staples. The incident occurred just a few hundred meters from the outskirts of the city.

“I didn’t hear it coming,” the woman, known only as Milena, told Le Monde. “I only had time to see its head 10 centimeters from me, and then, nothing, total blackout…”.

The woman was unconscious for about five minutes.

Another runner had been attacked days earlier. The incidents occurred near La Chapelle des Buis. Wildlife authorities described the behavior as highly unusual and authorized the animal’s removal. The cause of its aggression remains unclear.

A 71-year-old Winter Garden, Florida fisherman, Steven Hamilton, was posing for a photograph with a fish when a large alligator lunged from the water, seized his leg, and pulled him into a pond.

Industry observers note that emergency crews responded, but the alligator refused to let go of his body, according to Fox News. By the time they released him and killed the alligator, Hamilton was dead. The medical examiner identified drowning and blunt-force injury to his left leg as causes of death, with alligator tooth marks on both sides of the leg.

Sources indicate that alligator attacks are rare but occur occasionally. According to the Florida Fish & Wildlife Conservation Commission, there have been a total of 500 alligator bites against humans since 1948, including 32 fatal encounters.

Asiatic black bear. Photo: Shutterstock.

Vladimir Odulo, a fisherman from Primorye in Russia’s Far East, survived an attack by an Asiatic black bear, also known as a Himalayan bear.

The bear attacked while Odulo was fishing. He tried to defend himself with his fishing rod, but the animal knocked him into the water. Odulo continued fighting as it “beat his face like a boxer,” Russian media reported the fisherman saying. Suddenly, the bear stopped the attack and fled into the forest.

Odulo suffered several wounds and a serious eye injury, but survived. Doctors in Vladivostok were able to save his eyesight.

A venomous Caspian cobra, which now occurs high in Himachal Pradesh. Photo: Shutterstock.

Industry observers note that two deaths in the Indian Himalaya have been attributed to Caspian cobras. Native to Central Asia, this venomous species has expanded its range eastward into the higher reaches of Himachal Pradesh. It now also occurs in Pakistan and Kashmir.

According to recent reports, the first death occurred when a 40-year-old man accidentally stepped on a Caspian cobra while spraying an apple orchard. Wearing open-toed footwear, he sustained two bites on his leg. He was taken to a local faith healer before being shifted to the hospital, where he was declared dead, according to the Tribune of India.

In the second case, a 62-year-old man stepped on a snake while on his way to work and was bitten on the leg. He collapsed within half an hour and was taken to a health facility, where he died.

These fatalities occurred some time ago, but the report on them was published just this week in the journal Epidemiology International. The Caspian cobra generally inhabits higher, open, rocky terrain at elevations of 2,000m or higher, where both incidents occurred. Researchers suggest its range may now include lower elevations.

A charging elephant. Photo: Shutterstock.

Two men died in separate elephant attacks in northern Kenya.

On October 11, Eisimgai Gorow Ltarakwa, 41, was herding goats near Nguposorogin village when a lone elephant attacked him. He suffered severe injuries and died at the scene.

Two days later, Mukhtar Abdoy Hussein, 64, was grazing livestock near Benane village when a herd of elephants trampled him to death.

Recent findings suggest that the incident highlights the risks faced by herders in areas where livestock grazing activities bring communities into close proximity with wildlife. Under a conservation initiative, the families are entitled to receive compensation, according to Kenyan media.

Real Estate Crowdfunding Starts at $10 – Your Money Can Be Stuck for Months

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (499 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Real estate crowdfunding lets you buy into property funds for as little as $10.
  • It has been revealed that fundrise’s Equity REIT, a real estate investment trust, took no buyback requests from July 2025 until it merged into a larger fund, the Fundrise eREIT, in April 2026.
  • According to recent reports, say you put $5,000 into the Fundrise eREIT and need it back a year later.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Real estate crowdfunding lets you buy into property funds for as little as $10. Selling usually means waiting for the fund to buy your shares back, and funds cap those buybacks each quarter and sometimes halt them. Invest only money you can leave alone for five years, and keep it a small part of your portfolio.

It has been revealed that fundrise’s Equity REIT, a real estate investment trust, took no buyback requests from July 2025 until it merged into a larger fund, the Fundrise eREIT, in April 2026. RealtyMogul’s Income REIT and Apartment Growth REIT suspended buybacks that April and still weren’t taking requests in September.

According to recent reports, say you put $5,000 into the Fundrise eREIT and need it back a year later. Its quarterly report through September says it limits buybacks to 2.5% of its value a quarter, or up to 5% at its manager’s choice. Since the merger, investors had asked it to buy back about 17.9 million shares, and about 14 million of those shares were still waiting. Its prospectus also sets a 1% penalty on shares sold back within five years, $50 on a stake still worth $5,000.

Sources indicate that anyone can buy what these platforms sell to the public. Private deals usually take only accredited investors. The financial tests are income over $200,000 in each of the last two years and expected this year ($300,000 with a spouse or partner), or a net worth over $1 million not counting your home. Fees run about 1% a year. Fundrise charges a 0.85% management fee on its real estate funds plus a 0.15% advisory fee, and Arrived, which sells shares of single rental homes, builds its one-time fee for finding each house into the share price.

According to recent reports, hold most of your real estate money in a REIT index fund instead. Vanguard’s Real Estate ETF charges 0.13% a year against Fundrise’s 1% in fees and can be sold any trading day, though its price changes daily.

Before you invest, look up the fund on the SEC’s EDGAR site and open its latest annual report. Check it for suspended buybacks, and read the auditor’s report for a going-concern warning, which means the auditor doubts the organization can keep operating for another year. Arrived Homes, which holds the houses behind Arrived’s single-home shares, got one for 2025 because it was short of cash.

Pass on any offering whose latest report demonstrates either, however low its minimum.

The 101 money moves that matter most, from the foundations to protecting what you’ve built.

A 76-Year-Old Kazakh Blacksmith Is Walking Around the World

📅 21 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (974 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that sarsenbay Kotyrashov had never left his native Kazakhstan when, in 2023, he set out to walk across the Caucasus.
  • Now, three years later, Kotyrashov has almost 30,000 followers on Instagram who have tuned in for his journeys on foot across Eurasia.
  • Industry observers note that alongside his growing social media presence, Kotyrashov has been working with UNESCO to document Kazakh artisanal practices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that sarsenbay Kotyrashov had never left his native Kazakhstan when, in 2023, he set out to walk across the Caucasus. A blacksmith from the industrial province of Ulytau in central Kazakhstan, Kotyrashov had in tow only a battered suitcase and his signature leather hat as he crossed the Kazakh border. He was 73 years old.

Now, three years later, Kotyrashov has almost 30,000 followers on Instagram who have tuned in for his journeys on foot across Eurasia. People stop him and ask for selfies with Ulytauman, his online moniker and a reference to his home province.

Industry observers note that alongside his growing social media presence, Kotyrashov has been working with UNESCO to document Kazakh artisanal practices. He is now 76, and his travels are far from over.

It has been revealed that kotyrashov started his first job at age nine, working as a herder. By the time he entered his 70s, he had worked an astonishing diversity of manual labor jobs: carpenter, joiner, stonemason, lathe operator, metalworker, and most recently blacksmith. His expertise in traditional artisanship landed him a job at the Ulytau National Reserve Museum, a 150,000-hectare open-air museum comprising everything from mountains to mausoleums. From 2010 to 2020, Kotyrashov worked restoring historical buildings on the reserve, some of which date back to the Bronze Age.

The mausoleum of Jochi Khan, a 12th century Mongol ruler, is only one of the 25 building complexes at the Ulytau National Museum Reserve. Photo: Wikimedia Commons.

According to recent reports, tourists came from around the world to visit the reserve. Kotyrashov began to dream of traveling like them. “Why not?” he asked himself. “Why haven’t I seen the whole world myself? In my entire life, I’ve only ever seen Ulytau and Astana.”.

Then came the pandemic, and his wife of 40 years passed away. Kotyrashov built a small hand-cart and set out across Kazakhstan on foot. “I chose to travel on foot, because when you walk, you notice much more, including nature, landscapes, animals, and plants,” he explained. “There is also time to think, to reflect, and to understand things.”.

Kotyrashov’s first journey in 2022 was a love letter to Kazakhstan. As he walked from town to town over 181 days, pulling a homemade cart weighing around 60kg, he spoke with local artisans about their crafts. He tied a flag to his cart to promote the Qymyzmuryndyk festival, which celebrates the traditional Kazakh drink of kumis, or fermented mare’s milk. Local governments began holding press conferences for him and organizing lodging.

Photo: Sarsenbay Kotyrashov/Instagram.

Recent findings suggest that “Each day, I would meet with anywhere from 150 to 500 people in different parts of the country,” he told a Kazakh outlet. “The greatest discovery of my journey was the people — the citizens of Kazakhstan. They are generous, kind, noble, and open-hearted; I was truly struck by the kind of people who inhabit our Kazakhstan. It gives me hope for a better future.”.

Industry observers note that in 2023, he crossed the border into Russia, then followed the spine of the Caucasus Mountains through Chechnya and Georgia, and finally into Türkiye. Sometimes, he bivouacked in his sleeping bag. In towns, though, Chechen and Ingush Georgian locals invited him to stay with them. In Türkiye, he slept in mosques.

Industry observers note that kotyrashov decorated his cart with flags celebrating Kazakhstan. Photo: Kazinform.

Sources indicate that after his trip to Türkiye, Kotyrashov tackled China. Unlike in Central Asia and the Caucasus, he finally had to pay for hotels. By now, though, he had secured a trip coordinator and sponsors who helped him cover the costs. He took photos at the Great Wall and ended his journey in Beijing.

Europe posed greater difficulties. Everywhere else he had visited, he walked along the side of the highway. Unbeknownst to him when he began his 2026 trip, 3,000km from Belgrade to Paris, walking on highways is largely illegal in Europe. He had replaced his cart with an old suitcase, but the suitcase bit the dust on an unpaved footpath 150km outside Paris.

In a recent development, but Kotyrashov had an appointment. Determined to make it, he left the suitcase behind and sped on with his backpack.

On April 24th, he arrived at the UNESCO World Heritage Center in Paris and presented officials there with a handmade iron bell. At the Center, he met with Kazakhstan’s permanent UNESCO representative and shared his research on Kazakh artisanship and nomadic travel.

It has been revealed that kotyrashov on the Great Wall of China. Photo: Astana Times.

It has been revealed that after returning from Paris, Kotyrashov began working once more as a blacksmith to save up for his next trip. Sponsors help him with lodging and food, but he still needs to pay for his own gear. “Over the course of six months, I wore out seven pairs of shoes,” he noted.

In 2027, he will set out to another continent: the Americas. He aims to cross the United States from coast to coast, starting in Florida and ending in California. After his experience in Europe, he’s studying up on American highway law.

Recent findings suggest that three years ago, Kotyrashov left Kazakhstan for the first time. Now, he’s hoping the American trip will contribute to his broader goal of claiming a Guinness record for the most miles walked by a person over 75.

Industry observers note that “I had never traveled far in my life,” he said. “But it is never too late to travel.”.

Photo: Sarsenbay Kotyrashov/Instagram.

  • A 17-person team from the Archaeological Legacy Institute and Purdue University recently returned from Nikumaroro, a remote and uninhabited atoll in the Pacific Ocean.
  • Recent findings suggest that their primary objective was to investigate the Taraia Object, a mysterious shape in a shallow lagoon that researchers first noticed in 2020 on satellite and historical aerial photos.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A highly anticipated expedition to solve one of aviation’s greatest mysteries has concluded without finding the wreckage of Amelia Earhart’s missing plane.

A 17-person team from the Archaeological Legacy Institute and Purdue University recently returned from Nikumaroro, a remote and uninhabited atoll in the Pacific Ocean.

Recent findings suggest that their primary objective was to investigate the Taraia Object, a mysterious shape in a shallow lagoon that researchers first noticed in 2020 on satellite and historical aerial photos. While some hoped the anomaly was the remnants of Earhart’s Lockheed Electra, the expedition determined it was entirely natural.

The Taraia Object on a satellite image. Located at Nikumaroro. Photo: Archaeological Legacy Institute.

It has been revealed that according to Purdue University officials, the object was a cluster of large fallen trees resting on a sandbar. Much of the debris observed in satellite images had already broken up and washed away, leaving a single Y-shaped piece. The reflective, metallic glint seen from above turned out to be a hardened layer of coral sand coating the wood.

Sources indicate that on the way to the atoll. Photo: Purdue Research Foundation.

Recent findings suggest that the five-day operation proved logistically complicated. Workers faced dense brush and a large population of giant coconut crabs. The nocturnal activities of the massive crabs forced the crew to abandon aims to camp on the atoll and to return to the ship each evening. During the day, the crabs simply minded their own business.

One of the crew holds a coconut crab. Photo: Purdue Research Foundation.

Despite the difficulties, researchers recovered a few minor artifacts to study lagoon drift patterns, including a 76cm steel tube.

The team emphasized that ruling out the Taraia Object does not disprove the broader “castaway hypothesis.” For decades, historians have investigated the theory that Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan drifted off course during their 1937 global circumnavigation attempt, landing on Nikumaroro’s reef after failing to find Howland Island.

Amelia Earhart. Photo: amelia.prf.org.

Purdue University, where Earhart once served as a career counselor and aviation advisor, stated that its commitment to the search remains unchanged.

“Amelia Earhart never gave up — she kept pushing boundaries and flying into the unknown,” said Steve Schultz, Purdue’s general counsel and field assistant, after the expedition. “She kept flying, and we will keep searching.”.

For more details, extensive project documentation, and a gallery of expedition photographs, you can visit the official mission site at Amelia.prf.org.

Recent findings suggest that from left to right: Steve Schultz, Sirisha Bandla, and Marc Hagle, members of the research team. Photo: Purdue Research Foundation.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that “If I am good at something, it’s planning,” the 34-year-old German told ExplorersWeb.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that jost Kobusch is back in Nepal, preparing for the fourth round of his Everest project. His long-term goal is to climb solo in winter, without oxygen, self-supported, and via the Lho La and the West Ridge.

Sources indicate that “If I am good at something, it’s planning,” the 34-year-old German told ExplorersWeb. In this case, his blueprint is to arrive at the mountain in the best shape possible, physically and mentally.

According to recent reports, kobusch arrived in Kathmandu two weeks ago, together with friends Nicolas Scheidtweiler, Manuela Brummer, and photographer Alex Pichon. The group soon moved to Manang in the Annapurna region and began acclimatizing in the Chulu range.

Industry observers note that jost Kobusch (in yellow) scouts around Manang. Photo: Alex Pichon.

The plan was to spend a few nights at altitude and traverse the four Chulu peaks, all above 6,000m. “[However,] expeditions rarely unfold exactly as expected,” Kobusch admitted.

A member in the team felt exhausted after reaching the summit of the second peak, and the group abandoned the traverse there. “At least, we traversed from the summit of Chulu Far East (6,059m) to the top of Chulu East (6,444m) from the southeast,” Kobusch noted. He claims their line between the two peaks was latest.

According to recent reports, the line followed by Kobusch and his team up Chulu East. Photo: Alex Pichon.

Industry observers note that their next blueprint will be to climb a 7,000m peak in the area before Kobusch moves to the Khumbu in November. “I want to reach 8,000m, but on a different mountain than Everest, before the beginning of winter,” he noted.

According to recent reports, he wants to be completely acclimatized by the time he starts working on Everest on December 22, the start of calendar winter. Kobusch will have two photographers in Base Camp, but he will climb alone.

Acclimatization in Manang, Photo: Alex Pichon.

“I need to be able to move efficiently, make good decisions when I’m tired, manage risk alone, and stay comfortable in an environment where very small mistakes can have very serious consequences,” Kobusch recently wrote on social media. He claims that so far, all is going well. “I’m feeling good, I’ve done my homework, and I will start again on Everest better prepared than ever.”.

Kobusch has attempted winter Everest solo on three previous occasions, always via the Lho La and the West Ridge, thus avoiding venturing alone into the Khumbu Icefall.

In his first attempt in 2019-20, he reached the West Shoulder and pushed above 7,300m. On the second attempt in 2021-22, high winds didn’t let him go beyond 6,400m. He planned to try again the following year, but he caught dengue fever while training in Nepal and had to cancel.

Once recovered, he soloed Denali in February-March 2023. Everest had to wait one more year, this time due to a back injury. On the third attempt in 2024-25, he reached his highest point yet: 7,537m on December 27.

Kobusch’s highest point is shown with a green circle, and the Hornbein Couloir is the pink line on the 3D map by RealityMaps.

“The chances of success are not particularly high,” he recently wrote. “If I had to put a number on it, I would say around 20%. But that does not make the attempt meaningless. If anything, it is part of what makes it interesting.”.

Tech Report: Pay Student Loan Interest While in School – Start Repayment Owing Only What You Borrowed

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (471 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Unsubsidized federal loans and most private student loans charge interest from the day the money is paid out, even while you’re in class.
  • Recent findings suggest that federal student loans for undergraduates require no payments until six months after you leave school, which makes the interest easy to ignore.
  • In a recent development, subsidized and unsubsidized loans carry the same fixed rate, 6.52% on latest undergraduate loans, according to Federal Student Aid.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unsubsidized federal loans and most private student loans charge interest from the day the money is paid out, even while you’re in class. Pay that interest as it builds, in small payments to your loan servicer, and repayment starts from what you borrowed, not from a balance that grew all through school.

Recent findings suggest that federal student loans for undergraduates require no payments until six months after you leave school, which makes the interest easy to ignore. The Education Department covers it only on subsidized loans, which go to undergraduates with financial need.

In a recent development, subsidized and unsubsidized loans carry the same fixed rate, 6.52% on latest undergraduate loans, according to Federal Student Aid. Say a student borrows $5,500 at the start of each of four years at a round 6.5%, and her first bill comes six months after the fourth year ends. Her interest runs about $30 a month in the first year and about $119 a month by the fourth. Left unpaid, it adds up to about $4,300, so she starts repayment owing about $26,300 on the $22,000 she borrowed.

She owes that $4,300 either way, and carrying it into repayment costs more. Most private loans add unpaid interest to the principal, the amount you’re charged interest on, when repayment starts, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) states. From then on, it builds interest of its own. Federal loans don’t, but every payment covers unpaid interest before principal, so her $22,000 wouldn’t start shrinking until the $4,300 was paid.

Find your servicer, the manufacturer that handles your federal loans’ billing, in your StudentAid.gov account, where one is listed once your first loan is paid out. Set up a monthly payment that matches the interest, or send one payment a term from part-time pay.

According to recent reports, A private loan’s lender takes the same payments, since any student loan can be paid early without fees or penalties, the CFPB notes. Even a partial payment cuts the interest you’d carry into repayment, and it’s an easy way for a parent to help.

After graduation, aim any extra payments at principal so they don’t just push back your next due date.

Until then, ask your servicer for the monthly interest on each unsubsidized or private loan and pay that, about $5.40 for every $1,000 borrowed at 6.5%.
